question:
**In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

The student or the committee members writes every day.
solution:
The correct answer is **'writes every day.'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is grammatically incorrect.
 
• Here,** 'write every day' **should be used instead of **'writes every day'.**
 
• When a compound subject contains both a singular and a plural noun or pronoun **joined by "or" or "nor,"** the verb should agree with the part of the subject** that is closest to the verb. **This is also called the rule of proximity.
 
• Here, the closest subject is **'the committee members',** which **is plural.**
 
• Hence, we should use** 'write every day' **and not **'writes every day'** when a plural verb is needed.
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *The committee members or the student write every day. (Incorrect)*
 
• *The committee members or the student writes every day. (correct)*
 
 
 
• 
 
Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

**Correct Sentence:** *The student or the committee members** write every day.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• If the subject is joined by '**as well as', 'with', 'along with', 'together with', 'in addition to',** etc., the verb will agree with** the first subject.**
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *Silver as well as gold are a precious metal. (Incorrect)*
 
• *Silver as well as gold is a precious metal. (correct)*
